title: Landing conversion flow + messaging playtest
summary: Playtest doc mapping homepage sections to user intent and CTA sequencing. Microcopy variants + quick competitive notes to prioritize copy A/Bs for next sprint.
content:
Background:
This doc is a rapid playtest for homepage and primary product page messaging focused on conversion flow: first-touch -> evaluate -> prototype -> commit (hosted -> dedicated -> private). Goal: surface a small set of high-contrast hero/subhead/CTA variants tied to downstream funnel actions (signup, quickstart, request demo, enterprise contact).

Why this approach:
- We assume most visitors are engineers or platform buyers who self-qualify by behavior (open SDK, read pricing, check SLA docs).
- Messaging should map to the immediate action we want at that stage, not just a blanket claim.
- Test copy that nudges people into the correct path (self-serve vs sales-assisted).

High-level user intents and target CTAs:
1) Explore (curious devs) -> CTA: "Try the playground" or "Quickstart in 5 min"
2) Validate (prototype builders) -> CTA: "Run your model on our infra" or "Bring your model"
3) Scale / Enterprise -> CTA: "Get a capacity plan" or "Contact sales for Dedicated"
4) Security/compliance -> CTA: "Private deployment checklist" or "Request security brief"

Hero copy matrix (3 distinct tones to A/B):
A. Engineer-first, pragmatic
  - Hero: "Predictable inference. No surprises at scale."
  - Subhead: "Latency, cost, and reliability controls that let you ship LLM features with confidence."
  - Primary CTA: "Start a free quickstart"
  - Secondary CTA: "Compare hosting options"

B. Economic/ROI-forward
  - Hero: "Cut per-token cost — keep model quality."
  - Subhead: "Autoscaling, caching, and model routing that reduce unit cost without offline engineering."
  - Primary CTA: "See estimated savings"
  - Secondary CTA: "Run a cost simulation"

C. Platform/ops assurance
  - Hero: "Inference you can audit, scale, and SLA-guard."
  - Subhead: "Dedicated pools, private deployments, and fine-grained controls for regulated apps."
  - Primary CTA: "Request an SLA brief"
  - Secondary CTA: "Download security overview"

Notes on voice: keep copy concise, engineering-respectful (no marketing fluff). But test a slightly warmer ROI-forward tone as a second experiment — that can hit PMs/finance.

Microcopy and above-the-fold experiments (short lines to test):
- "Same API. From sandbox to SLA-backed production."
- "Move faster than building inference infra from scratch."
- "Pin model versions. Roll out safely."
- "Pay per inference or reserve capacity — predictable billing."

Primary product page (dedicated / private) modular sections:
- What you get (bullets): throughput guarantees, isolation, autoscale policy samples, PKI/KMS integrations.
- How it works: runtime + routing + caching (3-panel explainer with one-sentence summaries).
- Cost signals: unit economics, sample pricing scenarios, tradeoffs list.
- Trust section: compliance badges, customer logos, uptime SLA blurb.
- Next steps CTA flow: trial -> pilot -> contract.

Conversion flow mapping to analytics events (minimum viable):
- hero_cta_click -> which variant -> downstream funnel: signup_started -> quickstart_completed -> first_request
- pricing_modal_open -> time on pricing -> sampling of 'request-savings-report'
- security_assets_download -> request_sales -> enterprise_lead_tagged

Initial prioritization for copy experiments (week 1 sprint):
1) Two hero variants: A (Engineer-first) vs B (Economic). Measure hero_cta_click / signup_started.
2) Two primary CTAs for prototype stage: "Run your model" vs "Bring your model" (which implies upload vs bring-your-own). Hypothesis: fewer words = higher CTR.
3) Microcopy swap in feature bullets: 'predictable latency' vs 'predictable cost' to see which drives more pricing views.

Benchmarks and success metrics:
- Early signal: hero CTA CTR lift >= +10% compared to baseline copy in last deployment (baseline = current live homepage as of Oct 2025).
- Mid-funnel: signups -> 7-day activation (first 100 tokens) conversion lift +8%.
- Enterprise signal: demo requests sourced from product page increase by +15% (quality measured by MQL->SQL rate).

Competitive notes (quick scan, not exhaustive):
- Major managed LLM APIs: price-focused claims, easy-to-use SDKs. Weakness: less control over dedicated/private deployments and fewer enterprise ops assurances.
- Inference runtimes (self-hosted vendors): strong on control and customization but require infra ops and lack turnkey cost optimization / routing.
- Cloud-provider endpoint products: strong ecosystem fit, but higher per-token cost and limited model routing flexibility.
Implication: test copy emphasizing "control without ops tax" — that phrase resonates with platform buyers who fear maintenance debt.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Do we want a single primary CTA across all pages (simplicity) or contextual CTAs per user intent (complex)? Recommendation: contextual for hero variants, but include a persistent micro-CTA in header ("Try free") for low-friction access.
- Which pricing examples are granular enough to show without scaring buyers? Need finance input.
- Legal review required for any phrasing about SLAs and uptime numbers.

Notes to design/analytics/engineering:
- Design: provide hero art options that imply 'throughput' (visual metaphors: pipes, routing diagrams) vs 'savings' (graphs, dollar signs). Avoid overused robot imagery.
- Analytics: wire hero variant flag and event mapping into existing experiment framework. Tag experiments with "LNDG-hero-v2".
- Engineering: ensure quickstart flow can be instrumented to different target CTAs and that redirect parameters persist through signup.

Next steps (this doc is a working playbook):
- Lock two hero variants and three microcopy swaps by EOW (Nov 14, 2025) -> handoff to design for assets.
- Implement analytics events and run a 2-week experiment after deployment to traffic-split.
- Sync with finance/legal on any claims (savings % examples, SLA numbers).

Quick reference hero lines (copy deck for A/B):
- "Predictable inference. No surprises at scale."
- "Cut per-token cost — keep model quality."
- "Inference you can audit, scale, and SLA-guard."
- "Same API from sandbox to SLA-backed production."

Brainstorm fragments (notes to self):
- Consider a small interactive savings calculator on pricing page: input qps/seq_len model -> recommended hosting (hosted/dedicated/private) + estimated monthly saving vs raw cloud endpoint.
- Could experiment with micro-animations that show request routing fallbacks to build trust.

Slack thread references and context: see linked_confluence and Jira above.

Rough timeline: 3 sprints: copy lock + design (1), implement + analytics (1), run + analyze (1).

End of playtest doc.

Unpolished / notes to file: will iterate after design critique. Some phrasing is intentionally terse for rapid testing.
